{{nihongo||塵劫記|'''Jinkōki'''}} is a three-volume work on [[Japanese mathematics]], first edited and published by [[Yoshida Mitsuyoshi]] in 1627. Over his lifetime, Mitsuyoshi revised ''Jinkōki'' several times.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last1=Mitsuyoshi |first1=Y. |title=吉田光由『「塵劫記」初版本 影印、現代文字、そして現代語訳』 |last2=Sato |first2=K. |publisher=Kenkyūsha |year=2006 |isbn=978-4-87639-409-8 |language=ja |trans-title=First Edition of 'Jinkōki': Facsimile, Modern Characters, and Modern Translation}}</ref> The edition released in the eleventh year of the [[Kan'ei era]] (1641) became particularly widespread. The last version personally published by Mitsuyoshi was the ''Idai'' ({{lang|ja|井大}}), which came out in the eighteenth year of the Kan'ei (1634). Subsequent to that, various editions of ''Jinkōki'' were released, one of which includes ''Shinpen Jinkōki'' ({{lang|ja|新編塵劫記}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jinkoki: Japanese Mathematics in the Edo Period |url=https://www.ndl.go.jp/math/e/s2/1.html |access-date=2023-07-08 |website=www.ndl.go.jp |language=en}}</ref>

''Jinkōki'' is one of the most popular and influential Japanese mathematics books in history,<ref name=":1" /> having influenced [[Seki Takakazu]], [[Kaibara Ekken]], and many other later Japanese mathematicians.<ref name=":2">鳴海風「和算」『東京人』第321号、都市出版、52-56頁、2013年2月3日。</ref> It is partly based on the works of [[Yuan dynasty]] mathematicians in China.<ref name=":2" />

== Etymology ==
The name ''Jinkōki'' is derived from ''jintenkō'' ({{lang|ja|塵点劫}}), an immeasurably long span of time mentioned in the [[Lotus Sutra]],
hence the nuance of permanence in the [[Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese word]] ''jinkō'' and its reflection in English title.<ref name=":2" />

== Content ==
The book contained instructions for dividing and multiplying with a [[soroban]] and mathematical problems relevant to merchants and craftsmen. The book also contained several interesting mathematical problems, and was the first Japanese book to use [[Color printing|printing in colour]]. As a result, the Jinkōki became the most popular Japanese mathematics book ever and one of the most widely read books of the [[Edo period]]. Mitsuyoshi made reference to everyday problems, such as buying and selling [[rice]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Nishida |first=T. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2rgDPQAACAAJ |title=『塵劫記』にまなぶ |publisher=Kenkyusha |year=2005 |isbn=978-4-87639-138-7 |language=ja |trans-title=Learning from 'Jinkōki' |access-date=13 July 2023}}</ref>

The book was originally published in three volumes, the first of which mainly describes [[multiplication]] and [[Division (mathematics)|division]] using the soroban. The second and third volumes include an assortment of practical and recreational problems. The included problems are not arranged according to any specific order.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Yoshida |first1=M. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PbBHAAAACAAJ |title=吉田光由の『塵劫記』: 二十六条本の現代訳と変遷 |last2=Ōya |first2=S. |last3=Shoten |first3=I. |publisher= |year=1997 |isbn=978-4-87639-608-5 |language=ja |trans-title=Jinkōki, annotated by Shinichi Ōya, Iwanami Shoten |access-date=13 July 2023}}</ref>

The book includes ideas that aimed to keep readers from boredom by adopting a wide variety of problems such as calculations of areas of rice fields, problems related to the construction of rivers and riverbanks, geometric progression, and the [[Josephus problem]]. The Shinpen Jinkōki was the most widespread version among the copies of Jinkōki, and widely used as a textbook for use of the soroban throughout the Edo period.<ref>{{Citation |last=Sato |first=K. |chapter=The Jinkōki of Yoshida Mitsuyoshi |date=2013 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-4-431-54273-5_12 |title=Seki, Founder of Modern Mathematics in Japan |series=Springer Proceedings in Mathematics & Statistics |volume=39 |pages=173–186 |editor-last=Knobloch |editor-first=E. |editor-link=Eberhard Knobloch |access-date=13 July 2023 |place=Tokyo |publisher=Springer Japan |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-4-431-54273-5_12 |isbn=978-4-431-54272-8 |editor2-last=Komatsu |editor2-first=H. |editor3-last=Liu |editor3-first=D.|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In addition to fundamental knowledge such as numerical notation, units, and multiplication tables, it also included slightly more specialised topics, such as methods to find [[square roots]] and [[cube roots]], practical calculations of area, [[currency conversion]], and [[Interest (economics)|interest calculation]]. The content covers almost all arithmetic needed in daily life at that time, and it is a characteristic of the book that explanations are given using familiar topics, such as using the increase of mice as an example for [[geometric progression]].<ref name=":1" />

Many different versions were published, with slightly modified content, and by the time of the [[Meiji era]], over 400 editions of Jinkōki had been published.<ref>{{Cite web |title=東北大学デジタルコレクション詳細画面 |trans-title=Jinkōki |url=https://www.i-repository.net/il/meta_pub/G0000398tuldc_5100000062 |access-date=13 July 2023 |website=www.i-repository.net |publisher=Tokoku University}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
